manifest_status: PARTIAL — see `frozen_at_next_run`. Not yet a valid pre-registration.
authority: docs/specs/local-memory-curator.md §19.1 (required metrics) and §20 (acceptance bar: 'before the frozen labeled corpus is scored, a committed benchmark manifest records the corpus hash, generator/verifier/policy fingerprints, retry/TTL policy, included claim classes, and pre-registered thresholds')
rule: Everything under `frozen` is a measured or read fact, verifiable today by the command in `verify_with`.
Everything under `frozen_at_next_run` is NOT yet frozen. It is listed explicitly rather than omitted, because a pre-registration that is silently incomplete is worse than one that admits its gaps.
No scoring run may be reported against this manifest until `frozen_at_next_run` is empty and `manifest_status` reads FROZEN.
Thresholds are set by a human before the run and never edited after seeing results (eval/curator/README.md: 'Pre-registered. Do not tune these after seeing results.').

corpus.name: curator unit corpus (dev)
corpus.why_not_committed: Slices of the owner's real Claude Code transcripts. Redacted but private; `eval/curator/.gitignore` excludes units/, gold/, gold_sid/, gold_sid_prefix/, results/, units_manifest.json. The hashes below are the committable identity.
corpus.verify_with: cd eval/curator && find units -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs shasum -a 256 | shasum -a 256
corpus.note: units_manifest.json reports selected.total = 83 and carries 83 index rows, but only 80 unique files: three rows are exact duplicates (unit_249e3ba9-0000, unit_32b5ac8d-0000, unit_9e5056b9-0000). The corpus size for pre-registration is 80.

gold.verify_with: cd eval/curator && find gold -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs shasum -a 256 | shasum -a 256

assignment_lists.note: None of the three ends with a newline, so `wc -l` under-reports by one each. Union = 58 unique units, no overlap, no orphans.

sentence_id_reannotation.recall_ceiling: Only 162/230 (70.4%) gold items resolve to a sentence ID without prefix fallback; 205/230 (89.1%) with it. Any SID-contract recall number is capped accordingly, and the cap must be stated beside the number.

standing_caveats: This 58-unit set is the DEV set. It has been scored against repeatedly and can no longer measure generalization (eval/curator/README.md). A blind test set is a separate, unbuilt artifact.
n=5 gold-negative units cannot support a confidence interval. Abstention numbers are a directional smell test, not a measurement.

9 gold items are sourced from TOOL_RESULT blocks, which PARSER_V1 does not emit records for, so they are unreachable under the shipped parser and ungradable for source_role (the schema offers only user/assistant).

Three gold files carry labeler_notes recording items deliberately OMITTED because no term pair could be built that a correct paraphrase would reliably contain. The gold set is knowingly under-complete for paraphrase-fragile items — a documented recall ceiling, not a model failure.

prompt.byte_identity_test: prompt.rs::tests::template_matches_the_eval_harness_byte_for_byte — USER_TEMPLATE == this file, asserted in CI

schema.title: CuratorProposalsSid
schema.byte_identity_test: prompt.rs::tests::schema_matches_the_eval_harness_byte_for_byte — OUTPUT_SCHEMA_JSON == this file, asserted in CI

verifier_fingerprint.note: There is no RENDER_V1 constant and no separate canonicalization-version constant. RENDER_V1 is versioned implicitly by segmenter_version; canonicalization by identity_version. Recorded here so the absence is deliberate rather than an oversight.

gates.nli_gate: g10_score_entailment — records not_run in V1; no scorer is configured

retry_and_ttl_policy.note: defer_recovery_rate and defer_expiry_rate are defined against THIS policy. Changing any value invalidates both metrics and requires a new manifest version.

provider_contract.constrained_decoding: permanent — `format` carries the schema on every request
provider_contract.think: top-level `think: false` for any model advertising the thinking capability; omitted entirely for families that do not
provider_contract.canary: one known-answer unit per run before unit 1; failure aborts the run
provider_contract.unload: keep_alive 0 then /api/ps polled until the model is gone — verified, never inferred

redteam_corpus.executable_by: src-tauri/tests/curator_redteam_e2e.rs (17 tests, every manifest line claimed)

measured_baselines.disclaimer: These are FACTS from prior runs on the dev gold set, recorded so a threshold can be anchored to evidence. They are NOT thresholds and they are NOT acceptance criteria.

gemma3-12b-sid.caveat: gemma3 is not a thinking family, so `think` was omitted rather than sent false. Its reject profile is the inverse of every other model (1 G1 reject, 79 G2), which makes its low false-reject rate a different phenomenon, not a better one.

quote_contract_reference.note: The pre-SID baseline the sentence-ID contract was meant to beat. Same 58-unit gold set, scorer v2, reported in eval/curator/results/comparison_v2.md.

metric_definitions.note: Verbatim intent from spec §19.1. The `harness` field records whether eval/curator/score.py emits it today — four of the six do not exist yet.

generator_candidate_recall.spec: gold memory instances proposed by the generator before verification, divided by all gold memory instances
generator_candidate_recall.harness: NOT EMITTED. Derivable from score.py's admissible_candidate_count over the 230 gold items, but not computed.

verifier_false_reject_rate.spec: correctly formed labeled candidates whose gold disposition is ProposalReady or ReviewRequired but whose verifier outcome is terminal Rejected, divided by all such admissible labeled candidates; attribute every error to GateName and RejectCode
verifier_false_reject_rate.harness: EMITTED as `verifier_false_reject_rate`, but with a non-identical denominator: score.py's admissible set is 'candidates whose statement matches a gold item', because the gold set carries no disposition labels. Adjacent, not equal.
verifier_false_reject_rate.gap: The gold set must gain per-item gold dispositions before this metric means what the spec says it means.

verifier_over_escalation_rate.spec: labeled candidates whose gold disposition is ProposalReady but whose verifier disposition is ReviewRequired, divided by all gold ProposalReady candidates; attribute every escalation to GateName and ReviewCode, including OversizedEvidence separately from Synthesis
verifier_over_escalation_rate.harness: NOT EMITTED. score.py has no ReviewRequired notion; its only non-terminal flag is G3 and it is 0 in every run.

defer_recovery_rate.spec: deferred candidates that reach a non-deferred terminal outcome within the frozen retry/TTL policy, divided by all deferred candidates old enough to evaluate
defer_recovery_rate.harness: NOT EMITTED and not measurable by the Python harness — defer/retry lives in the Rust ledger (state.rs). Needs a run-ledger reader, not a scorer change.

defer_expiry_rate.spec: deferred candidates that reach ExpiredVisible without recovery, divided by all deferred candidates old enough to evaluate; still-pending candidates reported separately and excluded from both denominators until mature

end_to_end_candidate_recall.spec: gold memory instances that ultimately reach human review, divided by all gold memory instances
end_to_end_candidate_recall.harness: No exact equivalent. `post_gate_recall` is the de-facto stand-in (gold items claimed by a surviving proposal), but the harness has no review queue, so the two are only equal while every survivor reaches review — which is true in V1 and must be re-checked if that ever changes.

supporting_metrics_required_by_19_1: over-cap opaque-block citation count and RequireReview(OversizedEvidence) routing accuracy, with silent Pass and terminal Reject both counted as policy errors
polarity, modality, temporal, quantity, and action accuracy
false-negative rate from a predetermined audit sample
untouched approval, edit, and rejection rates
p50/p95 runtime, peak RAM, deferred backlog

frozen_at_next_run.why_not_frozen: The spec requires thresholds to be pre-registered but does not supply numbers — §19.1 and §20 name the six metrics and demand a threshold for each without setting one. Wave 4a will not invent an acceptance bar and present it as normative. A human sets these, per claim class, before the scoring run.

required_shape.rule: spec §20: 'every included claim class meets those pre-registered recall and verifier thresholds on the frozen corpus. Fail closed must not degenerate into fail empty.' A threshold set is invalid unless it constrains BOTH a floor on recall and a ceiling on false rejection for every included class.

frozen_at_next_run.anchoring_evidence: measured_baselines above. The strongest measured arm (qwen3-coder-30b-sid) sits at recall 0.209, false-reject 0.286, source_role 0.984.

frozen_at_next_run.why_not_frozen: No run_meta.json records a model digest as a first-class field. The only digests recoverable are 12-hex short forms scraped from the embedded `ollama ps` sample rows, and one results dir has no ps rows at all. A pinned generator fingerprint needs the full sha256 from /api/tags at run time.
frozen_at_next_run.fix: run_bench.py should record the served digest from /api/tags into run_meta.json; the Rust provider already pins it (ProviderConfig::model_digest) and aborts on mismatch.

frozen_at_next_run.why_not_frozen: run_meta.json records prompt/schema by PATH STRING only — no content hash, no git SHA, no scorer version. Reproducibility currently rests on the path not having changed underneath the result.
frozen_at_next_run.fix: stamp prompt_sha256, schema_sha256, git_sha, scorer_version, and units content_sha256 into run_meta.json.

frozen_at_next_run.why_not_frozen: generator_candidate_recall, verifier_over_escalation_rate, defer_recovery_rate and defer_expiry_rate have no implementation anywhere in the repo. A threshold cannot be pre-registered against a metric nothing computes.
frozen_at_next_run.fix: the first two are score.py changes; the last two need a reader over the Rust curator ledger (state.rs CuratorLedger) and cannot come from the Python harness at all.

frozen_at_next_run.why_not_frozen: The gold set labels statements and evidence, not dispositions. verifier_false_reject_rate and verifier_over_escalation_rate are both defined against a gold ProposalReady/ReviewRequired label that does not exist yet.
The 58-unit set is the DEV set by its own README and has been scored against repeatedly. A frozen labeled corpus for acceptance must be held out.
§19.1 requires both; neither the Python harness nor the Rust run audit records peak RSS today. Latency p50/p95 IS recorded.

untouched approval/edit/rejection rates, review time and queue burden are only observable once a human uses the review queue on real proposals. They belong to the Phase D observation window, not to a corpus score.

known_defects: units_manifest.json double-counts three units (83 rows, 80 files).
eval/curator/README.md line 7 references README-harness.md, which does not exist — the content was merged into README.md.
eval/curator/results/qwen3-coder-30b-sid/metrics.md has two columns headed `qwen3-coder:30b` (the SID run and the older quote-contract run); the columns cannot be told apart from the header alone.
anchor_comparison.md predates scorer v2: no CIs, no source_role row, and its `verifier_false_reject_est` is the deprecated v1 formula whose denominator grows with every piece of junk a model emits.
Shipped defaults diverge from every benchmark setting: keep_alive 10m (code) vs 30m (runs), timeout_unit_secs 180 (code) vs 120-900 (runs). num_predict is not recorded in any run_meta.json.
